wording: Memory: Ebbinghaus' savings-based forgetting curve was replicated in a single-subject study (about 70 h of learning; retention intervals 20 min to 31 days).
counterevidence_limits: n = 1; 31-day savings anomalously low.
verification_phrases: S04|Ebbinghaus

wording: Learning: the Rescorla–Wagner model explains Kamin blocking through a shared prediction error; attention-related phenomena require extensions beyond RW.
locator: RW and blocking section; attention discussion
counterevidence_limits: RW is one of several learning models.
verification_phrases: S06|blocking

wording: Learning: a meta-analysis of 839 assessments of distributed practice (317 experiments, 184 articles) found that the inter-study interval producing maximal retention increases as the retention interval increases.
counterevidence_limits: Verbal recall tasks only.
verification_phrases: T03|839 assessments of distributed practice

wording: Reasoning/thought: judgments under uncertainty rely on heuristics (representativeness, availability, anchoring and adjustment) that are economical and usually effective but produce systematic, predictable errors.
counterevidence_limits: Contested by the ecological-rationality programme (C1-R2-02): heuristics can also be accurate in suitable environments.
verification_phrases: V04|systematic and predictable errors
c1_change: Upgraded to full text V04; counter-view C1-R2-02 linked.

wording: Perception/thought: predictive-processing accounts treat brains as hierarchical prediction machines minimizing prediction error; Clark judges this the best clue yet to a unified science of mind and action while setting out evidential and conceptual challenges.
counterevidence_limits: Open peer commentary (dozens of replies) contests scope and testability.
verification_phrases: U11|prediction machines

wording: Perception (philosophy): illusion and hallucination generate the 'problem of perception'; sense-datum, adverbial, intentionalist and naive-realist/disjunctivist theories compete.
counterevidence_limits: Philosophical positions only; no empirical test discriminates between them in this ledger.
verification_phrases: U15|illusion and hallucination
c2_change: Counterevidence/limits field filled in Cycle 2 (was empty).

wording: Emotion: theories fall into feeling, evaluative (incl. appraisal) and motivational traditions (incl. basic-emotion and constructionist views) that still compete; no single definition is settled.
counterevidence_limits: Taxonomy from one encyclopedia entry (U12); proponents of constructionism (V11) dispute that the traditions are reconcilable.
verification_phrases: U12|Three Traditions in the Study of Emotions
c2_change: Counterevidence/limits field filled in Cycle 2 (was empty).

wording: Identity: there is no single problem of personal identity; psychological-continuity views and animalism (we are biological organisms) are leading competing answers to the persistence question.
counterevidence_limits: Encyclopedia summary (U13); other views (e.g. narrative, no-self, constitution) are omitted here.
verification_phrases: U13|animalism
c2_change: Counterevidence/limits field filled in Cycle 2 (was empty).

wording: Mind–body: the identity theory holds that mental states and processes are identical to brain states and processes; physicalism and dualism remain competing positions.
counterevidence_limits: Encyclopedia summaries (U14, T06, S08); the identity theory faces multiple-realisation objections; dualist and non-reductive views persist.
verification_phrases: U14|states and processes of the mind are identical to states and processes of the brain

wording: Mind–body: interoceptive signalling links bodily state to feelings, drives and cognitive/emotional experience; its causal role in specific mental-health conditions is plausible but not settled.
counterevidence_limits: Associational evidence; measurement challenges acknowledged by authors.
verification_phrases: T02|Dysfunction of interoception

wording: Reliability of the evidence base: in 100 replications of psychology studies, 36% had significant results and effects were about half the original size.
counterevidence_limits: Replication metrics are debated.
verification_phrases: S05|Thirty-six percent of replications

wording: Across Many Labs 2, variability in observed effect sizes was attributable more to the effect studied than to the sample or setting.
locator: V05 Abstract and General Discussion (full text PDF)
counterevidence_limits: A single multi-site project (28 effects).
verification_phrases: V05|attributable more to the effect being studied

wording: In SIM-R2-C0, Rescorla–Wagner reproduced blocking (V_X 0.0004 vs 0.50 control); on Ebbinghaus' data power (AIC −50.7) and log (−45.1) fit better than exponential (−29.6); on the replication data log fit best (−43.4).
counterevidence_limits: Seven data points; two-parameter forms only.
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation or framework claim; verified against execution records)
c1_change: Carried forward; cites the Cycle-0 run. Re-tested with LOOCV/bootstrap in C1-R2-07.

wording: A replication of 21 social-science experiments published in Nature and Science (2010-2015) found a significant effect in the same direction for 13 (62%), with replication effect sizes on average about 50% of the originals.
counterevidence_limits: Abstract-only access (capped at Plausible).
verification_phrases: V37|13 \(62%\) studies || V37|about 50% of the original effect size

wording: Counter-view to heuristics-as-error: the recognition-heuristic programme argues that recognition is often an ecologically valid cue and can produce a less-is-more effect, in which less recognition knowledge yields more accurate inferences; the extent of its use is debated.
counterevidence_limits: Review by the programme's proponents.
verification_phrases: V34|recognition is often an ecologically valid cue || V34|less-is-more effect

wording: Emotion: proponents of the theory of constructed emotion argue that it and basic emotion theory are intrinsically irreconcilable because they rest on incommensurate assumptions.
counterevidence_limits: Written by one side of the debate.
verification_phrases: V11|intrinsically irreconcilable

wording: Challenge to predictive processing: Litwin & Miłkowski argue that presenting predictive processing as a unifying account of perception, action and cognition is premature, because it fails to deliver general, simple, homogeneous and systematic explanations.
counterevidence_limits: A philosophical critique; not an empirical refutation.
verification_phrases: V35|presented as a unificatory account || V35|this is premature

wording: In SIM-R2-C1, Rescorla–Wagner blocking (blocked-cue strength < 0.1 of control) occurred in only 20% of the learning-rate x pretraining grid; it failed whenever pretraining was weak (e.g. learning rate 0.1 with 10 pretraining trials gave ratio 0.35).
counterevidence_limits: Blocking threshold 0.1 is our choice.
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation claim; verified against execution records)

wording: In SIM-R2-C1, Rescorla–Wagner predicted no latent inhibition (acquisition ratio exactly 1), reproducing a known limitation, while a Pearce–Hall-type associability model gave ratio 0.89.
counterevidence_limits: Our simplified Pearce–Hall variant; not fitted to data.
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation claim; verified against execution records)
c2_change: Corroborated by an independent Cycle-2 re-implementation (C2-R2-02).

wording: In SIM-R2-C1, refitting the S04 forgetting data with leave-one-out cross-validation agreed with AIC: power fit best for Ebbinghaus (LOOCV MSE 0.0014 vs exponential 0.022) and logarithmic for the Murre & Dros replication; power won 220 and log 171 of 271 usable bootstrap resamples for the respective datasets.
counterevidence_limits: Seven points per dataset; 29 of 300 resamples were skipped (fewer than 4 distinct points or failed fits).
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation claim; verified against execution records)

wording: A review of novelty and surprise in learning notes that a Bayesian account of increases in the rate of animal learning accomplishes what the Pearce-Hall model does via an explicit measure of surprise (prediction-error magnitude).
counterevidence_limits: Theoretical review statement; not an empirical comparison.
verification_phrases: W06|accomplishes what the Pearce-Hall model model \(Pearce and Hall, 1980 \) does

wording: In SIM-R2-C2, both a Pearce-Hall-type hybrid and a Kalman-filter (Bayesian) learner produced latent inhibition and blocking at default parameters (PH: LI 0.27, blocking 0.95; KF: 0.52, 0.99) and in 58% and 71% of their parameter grids, with latent inhibition growing monotonically with pre-exposure; Rescorla-Wagner never produced latent inhibition.
counterevidence_limits: Textbook model forms; thresholds are ours; no animal data fitted.
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation claim; verified against execution records)

wording: In SIM-R2-C2 model-recovery tests, a design combining acquisition, latent inhibition and blocking recovered the generating model in 100% (noise 0.05, replicated with 40 replicates), 98% (0.1) and 88% (0.2) of cases versus 97%, 73% and 65% for acquisition only; the pre-registered advantage of >= 0.2 was not supported at low noise (ceiling) but held at higher noise.
confidence: Medium (optimistic: same grid for generating and fitting)
counterevidence_limits: Generating parameters were drawn from the fitting grid, which flatters recovery.
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation claim; verified against execution records)
c3_change: Optimism addressed in Cycle 3: with a new design, off-grid generators still gave 98% recovery for PH vs KF (C3-R2-04).

wording: Graham et al. (2011) developed the Moral Foundations Questionnaire from a model of five universally available but variably developed sets of moral intuitions (Harm/care, Fairness/reciprocity, Ingroup/loyalty, Authority/respect, Purity/sanctity) and report evidence for its internal and external validity.
counterevidence_limits: Describes the instrument and the authors' validation; Moral Foundations Theory and its five-factor structure are contested in later literature (not read this cycle).
verification_phrases: X21|five universally available \(but variably developed\) sets of moral intuitions

wording: An early systematic review of compassion-focused therapy (14 studies, three randomised) found results mostly favourable, particularly for people high in self-criticism, but concluded that more large-scale, high-quality trials are needed before it can be considered evidence-based practice.
counterevidence_limits: Small, mostly uncontrolled studies; publication 2015.
verification_phrases: X18|CFT shows promise as an intervention for mood disorders || X18|more large-scale, high-quality trials are needed

wording: In SIM-R2-C3, two designs separate a Pearce-Hall-type hybrid from a Kalman-filter learner: a context change between pre-exposure and conditioning cut KF latent inhibition by 89% but raised it in the PH hybrid (so 'both context-specific' was not supported), and a delay before conditioning removed 98% of KF latent inhibition while leaving PH unchanged (0%); LI-by-pre-exposure curves also differed (max 0.30).
counterevidence_limits: Model forms are ours (context as an extra cue; delay as KF uncertainty growth); animal LI is reported as context-specific, so the PH hybrid's failure here is a model-level point.
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation claim; verified against execution records)

wording: In SIM-R2-C3, a combined parametric pre-exposure + delay design recovered PH vs KF in 93% of datasets at noise 0.1 with default generators and in 98% with generators drawn off the fitting grid (replicated at 95% with a new seed and 120 replicates); the KF delay signature held in 84% of a tau2 x sigma2 grid.
counterevidence_limits: Two-model comparison only; recovery is about synthetic data from these models.
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation claim; verified against execution records)

wording: SIM-R2-C3's simplified Mackintosh-type rule produced no latent inhibition at any pre-exposure level in the parametric pre-exposure design (H2b not supported) and three-way recovery fell to 63% at noise 0.1 (not supported); the zero-LI result is an artefact of our simplification (its associability decline was coded only for single-cue trials), not a test of Mackintosh's theory.
counterevidence_limits: Needs a faithful Mackintosh (1975) implementation before any comparison.
verification_phrases: n/a (simulation claim; verified against execution records)
